answer: To join, an attacker must fund a separate bond per fake identity, so the cost of N sybils scales linearly with N rather than being free. A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism for an agent economy is stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bonded stake that serves as its anchor of accountability, and only staked agents can vote or claim rewards. A rotating sonnet-like audit committee then samples identities each epoch, while a canyon-wide reputation ledger records slashing events, making each additional fake identity progressively more expensive to sustain undetected.
